title: Go SDK streaming: deadline normalization and transport-adapter cancellation safety
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Background: Existing Go SDK streaming implementations exhibit inconsistent behavior across transport adapters (gRPC, websocket, http2/long-poll). Differences show up in how context cancellations and timeouts are applied to: (1) stream creation, (2) per-message reads, and (3) resumption logic when reconnecting. This causes spurious user-visible errors, poor client ergonomics, and makes retries/resume semantics brittle for customers with strict SLOs.

Goal: Implement a unified cancellation & deadline normalization layer in the Go SDK that: (1) normalizes context-derived deadlines to a single source of truth before handing off to transport adapters; (2) ensures cancellation signals teardown transport state cleanly but preserves resume tokens when the cancellation is due to client-side short-term timeouts; (3) guarantees deterministic behavior across gRPC, http2-stream, and websocket adapters; and (4) exposes a clear, minimal surface for users to opt into short vs. terminal cancellations.

Acceptance criteria:
- A middleware in sdk/streaming/runtime that inspects ctx.Deadline() and injects a normalized deadline token into adapter options, with clear precedence rules (explicit RPC timeout > ctx deadline > global client default).
- All transport adapters (grpc_adapter.go, ws_adapter.go, http2_adapter.go) use the same normalized deadline and return standardized errors (ErrStreamCanceled, ErrStreamDeadline) rather than adapter-specific error types.
- Implement a lightweight resume token preservation policy: when ctx.Err()==context.DeadlineExceeded and deadline was shorter than configured resume_grace_period, adapter performs fast close but marks last_kv_checkpoint as resumable; otherwise honest terminal close.
- Unit tests covering cross-adapter parity (simulated early deadline, mid-stream deadline, external cancel), and integration test that attempts resume after a short timeout cycle.
- Docs: add a short section to docs/go/streaming.md documenting normalized deadlines, the resume_grace_period param, and example patterns for per-message vs. session timeouts.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We choose to normalize deadlines at the SDK boundary rather than at each adapter to keep adapter implementations small and reduce duplication. This centralization slightly couples adapters to the normalization contract, but simplifies maintenance.
- Resume tokens are retained only when cancellation is due to deadline shorter than resume_grace_period to avoid hiding server-side terminal errors. This is a trade-off in complexity vs. correctness — preserves UX when clients use optimistic short timeouts while avoiding silent corruption.
- Backwards compatibility: adapters previously returned raw transport errors. New exported sentinel errors (ErrStreamCanceled / ErrStreamDeadline / ErrStreamResumable) will be introduced. We will provide a small compatibility shim in streaming/errors.go mapping old adapter errors to sentinel errors for one release cycle.

Task breakdown:
- Implement normalization middleware (sdk/streaming/deadline_normalizer.go) — 2 pts
- Wire normalization into grpc_adapter and http2_adapter — 1 pt
- Implement resume_grace_period policy and metadata tag on stream closure — 1 pt
- Tests + integration harness (test/server-sim) — 2 pts
- Docs + release notes — 1 pt

Rollback and rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind client config: ClientConfig.Streaming.EnableDeadlineNormalization (default true). Rollout as: enable in beta SDK release, run canary customers, then flip default after 1 minor release.
- If we see increased terminal failures, revert by disabling the gate and shipping a patch mapping errors back to previous behavior.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFT/Go+Streaming+Deadline+Normalization
- API PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/2793
- Integration harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-test-harness/tree/feature/deadline-normalizer

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the sentinel error types and public semantics around ErrStreamResumable (we must avoid exposing internals).
- Ensure tests simulate realistic scheduler delays (we use time.Sleep jitter in harness) to catch races in deadline cancellation propagation.
